claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as lacking any in-game tutorial, requiring external guides to understand basic survival mechanics.

citations.review_text: First of all, it is not an easy game, there is no tutorial at all. I had to watch several hours of videos, to understand the basics. I don't have much hours and experience in the game yet, but I feel like I'm getting better. I don't starve to death in the first 20 minutes. When I stabbed a zombie in the back with a knife for a backpack just to carry more items and did it in silence....that was a great experience, hell yeah.

It is hard. I love it. It's definitely a grind not meant for the faint of heart. I have starved to death, cut myself on a fence and bled out, and watched to the sun from a middle of a lake while I accepted my inevitable fate. If you have the gajones to accept the learning curve, the game is a very rewarding experience.

Keep in mind, there is no end game event (at least as far as I know right now). The whole point of the game is keeping your dude or dudette alive in an insanely large open world, facing hostile players who want your shit, and zombies that want to eat your face. That grind I mentioned earlier? Loot is not easily come by. On top of that, there is a lot of trial and error with learning all the uses for items and their combinations. YouTube tutorials help, which I recommend for the basics of getting going. 

Playing with your friend is a little bit difficult, unless you know the maps like you live there. You can spawn into the same server as your friend, but it's up to you to track them down, which can be difficult.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the vanilla launcher and server browser as messy, unintuitive, and difficult to use for connecting to games.

citations.review_text: I can understand the appeal of the game loop, that's not the issue actually. The issue is how unintuitive and messy the vanilla launcher is. Official vanilla servers are genuinely a hellscape of cheaters since there is no moderation. Community servers can be dependency hell depending on the mods you try to use. And not to mention you are almost required to use a 3rd party launcher to effectively select servers. Servers will have low ping, but you try and connect and it can't establish a connection. Finally, depending on how you have your anti-virus setup it can be a nightmare trying to configure mod files.
Would rather play this on xbox (which is absolutely laughable). Game is trash on PC. Horrible launcher, horrible mod system, horrible coding. Literally a disaster.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe extended periods of walking and travelling across the map with minimal activity between player encounters.

citations.review_text:
I've been playing DayZ since October 2019, and it's still one of my favorite survival games. What makes DayZ stand out to me is the atmosphere and how unpredictable every encounter can be. You could spend hours travelling across the map without seeing anyone, then suddenly run into another player and have no idea whether they're friendly or hostile.

I really enjoy exploring, searching for supplies and trying to survive. The game does a great job of making you feel like you're actually living through a zombie outbreak.

However, one thing that has always bothered me is how slow the game can get. Sometimes DayZ genuinely feels like a walking simulator, especially when travelling across such a massive map with very little happening along the way.

I also think DayZ is at its best when playing modded. There's so much more freedom, customization and variety, with different servers offering completely different experiences. Whether it's additional weapons, vehicles, clothing or gameplay changes, modded servers give players so many more options. However, if you prefer a more hardcore survival experience, vanilla is still a great choice. The base game is challenging enough, and different maps can completely change how you approach survival. For example, Badlands introduces extreme heat as another survival challenge, making water management and preparation much more important.

Of course, the game still has its fair share of bugs, glitches and server issues, which can sometimes become frustrating.

Despite its flaws, DayZ is still a game I keep coming back to. After playing since 2019, I've had plenty of memorable experiences, and there's something about its atmosphere and survival gameplay that other games haven't quite managed to recreate.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe mechanics involving survival health statuses such as contracting cholera from unpurified water.

citations.review_text:
Extremely shortened version of how I died on my 12 hour character DayZ

At the time of the start of my slow death, I was well equipped with good clothing, food, water, and two guns fully loaded. I was in the wilderness and filled my water without purifying it.

I contracted Cholera.

Out of desperation, I wandered looking for Tetracyclin and Multivitamins. I successfuly found them after wandering the coast for an hour. 

Fast forward an hour later, I contracted it again. Cholera forced me to drink and eat in very small portions. I made it to a downslope part of a forest, then I heard it.

Wolves.

At this point, I had no water or food. The wolves attacked me, but thanks to my silenced pistol and sniper, I was able to survive by the skin of my teeth. I knew my time was up. No meds, no food, no water. 

I shot myself. It was over too quick.

9.5/10

This is a great game, very in depth systems of hunger, thirst, temperature, health, and blood pressure. highly recommend, probably the best online survival game I've ever played. Very fun gameplay loop, but sometimes it's easy to rage quit.

claims.claim: Reviewers note the presence of cheaters on open and official servers.

citations.review_text: There are way too many cheaters

I have played DayZ since Arma 2 mod (different account).  What brings me back to dayz? Is it the best graphic and best shooter out there? No, its clunky and still has some arma carry over to it instead of that fluid feel. So what brings me back?  A non linear story, you make your own story. You make your own friends and groups, you play to anyway you want.  You only truly experience DayZ through community servers.  Dayz Mod Arma 2 was the same way, (BMRF) was the main chernarus server along with epoch, and Dayz origins, all community ran or in origins case, made.  

So if you want a game that truly lets you play any way you see fit, go for it.  Yes there is the occasional unfair players that cheat or exploit. Yes, the game is dated, and clunky, but not horrible.  The people and the community is what will make you easily see past all that.  

Good luck out there if you purchase it,  I know you wont regret it.  Expansion packs, wait for sales or just try the base game first.  Chernarus is still probably the most balanced most played.  If you want a desert map without  paying for the new badlands, Takistan or similar offered it, but they have players surge to it for about 3-6 months, then they always come back to Chernarus.  So may your experience, friends and journeys be memorable, and I hope i get to run into someone who read this, and rob them...maybe...possibly....likely...whats in that backpack?

Way to many cheaters in this game i only play on low end server pop less cheaters to dill with but that's not always the case one night i was on an Vanilla Lavonia server in the dark in the rain in the open field had a ballistic helmet and a ballistic vest I dies in one hit by a magic bullet when DayZ 2 comes out I'm not going to buy a crap game that cheaters are just going to ruin it cheaters world wide needs to be fin 25k $ plus put in prison for using hacks-under codes hackers are terrorists.

Dayz can be fun on a heavily moderated community run server, especially RP servers. If you're playing with a group of friends, this is a good game for a group. If you're playing solo, it's probably not going to be a good time. Open servers are just packed with cheaters, so avoid those unless you are into respawning. The game developers really should put more attention into preventing cheating, but it's been years now and they just can't seem to do anything about it. You can just run the game solo on your own private server, which isn't a bad idea for at least learning the maps and locations. After awhile the default game that is unmodded becomes sort of solved and becomes boring. Modded games are where things get interesting, some of the mods are much better than work done by the developer of the game. 

Overall the game is pretty good, but it is far from perfect, and I would really only recommend getting it on sale with none of the DLCs.
